source_text: Impleveras enim hoc sermone aliquid, contra quod si fuisses locutus ulterius, nimium impudens; sin autem omnia continenter, vel tarde posses apparere correctior. Nunc vero me dicis fallere, qui quod obieci, per te probo; et tu statim in eo, quod te putas consequenter instruxisse, mentiris. Ais quippe: Non liberum negamus arbitrium; et subiungis testimonium Evangelii, sed " vos Filius li raverit - ait Veritas - tunc vere liberi eritis " [n183] . Cum hoc in illo loco a Domino nostro Iesu constet in liberum arbitrium non fuisse prolatum, cuius expositionem sententiae paululum differentes, definitionibus et divisionibus, quid nostrum alteruter sentiat, explicemus. Debet quippe, secundum omnium doctorum disciplinam, inchoatio disputationis a definitione sumi.
pass_a_gloss: For by this speech you would have filled something, against which if you had spoken further, too shameless; but if all things continuously, you could appear even late more corrected. Now however you say that I deceive, I who prove through you what I objected; and you at once in that which you think you have constructed consequently, lie. You say indeed: We do not deny free choice; and you join a testimony of the Gospel, but If the Son shall have freed you — Truth says — then you will be truly free. When it stands that this in that place was not brought forth by our Lord Jesus against free choice, whose explanation of the sentence postponing a little, by definitions and divisions let us unfold what each of us senses as ours. For according to the discipline of all teachers, the beginning of a disputation ought to be taken from a definition.

lemmas.lexica: LS arbitrium=judgment, free decision; Blaise liberum arbitrium
LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere

pass_b_english: By this statement you would have established something definite. If you had then spoken against it, you would have appeared exceedingly shameless; if you had consistently maintained it throughout, you might have appeared corrected, even if belatedly. But now you say that I deceive, although I prove my charge through your own words; and you immediately lie in what you think you have constructed consistently. You say: “We do not deny free choice”, and append the Gospel's testimony: “But Truth says, ‘If the Son sets you free, then you will be truly free’” (John 8:36). Yet it is established that our Lord Jesus did not utter those words in that passage against free choice. Let us postpone their explanation a little and use definitions and distinctions to make clear what each of us means. According to the teaching of all learned people, a discussion ought to begin with a definition.

choices.why: Glossary default: arbitrium is the decision-power, not a later Augustinian/Reformation free-will locus.
Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.
